name: Job
lede: The eighteenth book of the Bible, in full: a man in the land of Uz, perfect and upright, stripped of all he had; his three friends and their counsel; Elihu; Jehovah answering out of the whirlwind; and the latter end of Job blessed more than his beginning, every word in the words of the ASV.

books.name: The Land of Uz
books.blurb: A man in the land of Uz, perfect and upright, with seven sons and three daughters and the greatest substance of the children of the east; Satan before Jehovah — doth Job fear God for nought?; four messengers, each escaped alone to tell thee; Jehovah gave, and Jehovah hath taken away; the boils, the potsherd and the ashes; three friends sitting silent seven days; then Job opened his mouth: let the day perish wherein I was born.

books.name: The Vision of the Night
books.blurb: Eliphaz the Temanite: who ever perished, being innocent?; a spirit passed before my face — shall mortal man be more just than God?; man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward; happy is the man whom God correcteth. Job answers: oh that my vexation were but weighed; my brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook; my days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle; what is man, that thou shouldest magnify him?

books.name: No Umpire Betwixt Us
books.blurb: Bildad the Shuhite: doth God pervert justice?; inquire of the former age; can the rush grow up without mire?; whose trust is a spider's web. Job answers: how can man be just with God? — he maketh the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades; he goeth by me, and I see him not; there is no umpire betwixt us; thou hast fashioned me as clay; the land of darkness and of the shadow of death.

books.name: If a Man Die
books.blurb: Zophar the Naamathite: canst thou by searching find out God? — it is high as heaven, deeper than Sheol. Job answers: no doubt but ye are the people; ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; behold, he will slay me, nevertheless I will maintain my ways; man, that is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble; there is hope of a tree; if a man die, shall he live again?

books.name: My Witness Is in Heaven
books.blurb: Eliphaz again: should a wise man fill himself with the east wind?; art thou the first man that was born?; the wicked man travaileth with pain all his days. Job answers: miserable comforters are ye all; his archers compass me round about; O earth, cover not thou my blood — even now, behold, my witness is in heaven; who is there that will strike hands with me?; the bars of Sheol.

books.name: My Redeemer Liveth
books.blurb: Bildad again: the light of the wicked shall be put out; a gin shall take him by the heel. Job answers: he hath walled up my way; my kinsfolk have failed; have pity upon me, O ye my friends; oh that my words were graven in the rock for ever! — but as for me I know that my Redeemer liveth. Zophar again: the triumphing of the wicked is short; the viper's tongue; the bow of brass.

books.name: Where I Might Find Him
books.blurb: Job: wherefore do the wicked live? — their children dance, they sing to the timbrel and harp; they lie down alike in the dust. Eliphaz the third time: is not thy wickedness great?; acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace. Job: oh that I knew where I might find him! — I go forward, but he is not there; when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold; the poor of the earth, wet with the showers of the mountains.

books.name: The Price of Wisdom
books.blurb: Bildad the last time: how much less man, that is a worm! Job: he hangeth the earth upon nothing; these are but the outskirts of his ways; till I die I will not put away mine integrity from me. Surely there is a mine for silver — but where shall wisdom be found? It cannot be gotten for gold; the price of wisdom is above rubies; God understandeth the way thereof: behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom.

books.name: The Months of Old
books.blurb: Oh that I were as in the months of old, when his lamp shined upon my head — the seat in the gate, eyes to the blind and feet to the lame. But now they that are younger than I have me in derision; I am a brother to jackals, and a companion to ostriches; my harp is turned to mourning. I made a covenant with mine eyes; let me be weighed in an even balance; lo, here is my signature. The words of Job are ended.

books.name: Elihu
books.blurb: Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, young, his wrath kindled: I am young, and ye are very old; my breast is as new wine-skins ready to burst; God speaketh in a dream, in a vision of the night — I have found a ransom; far be it from God, that he should do wickedness; who giveth songs in the night; behold, God is great — the clouds, the lightning, the snow and the ice; out of the north cometh golden splendor.
